Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat

Class ChatTurnContext

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.ChatTurnContext
@Component @Scope(value="request", proxyMode=TARGET_CLASS) public class ChatTurnContext extends Object
Per-turn context bag carrying the parent agent id and parent owner so the Spring AI tool callback (US-12-003 DelegateTool) can resolve "which chat turn am I running in" without depending on SendMessageService or threading a context object through every Spring AI tool layer.

Lifecycle: SendMessageService populates an instance at the start of each turn (immediately before invoking ChatRequestBuilder.build(...)) and clears it on completion via Flux.doFinally(...) — covers normal completion, errors, and cancellation.

Scope: Spring request scope with a CGLIB target-class proxy so singleton beans (SendMessageService, DelegateTool) can inject it. Each HTTP request — and thus each chat turn — gets its own instance; concurrent turns on different requests cannot see each other's context. The SSE SseEmitter path stays inside the request thread until the controller returns, which is what makes the request scope reachable from inside the synchronous Spring AI tool callback.

Defensive access: parentAgentId() and parentOwner() throw IllegalStateException if the context has not been entered — invocation of DelegateTool outside of a chat turn is impossible by construction (the LLM cannot legally emit a tool call without an in-flight turn), so the thrown exception is operator-debug, not user-facing.

  • Method Details

    • enter

      public void enter(AgentId parentAgentId, UserId parentOwner)
      Populate the context for the in-flight turn. Subsequent parentAgentId() / parentOwner() calls return these values until clear() is invoked.

    • clear

      public void clear()
      Reset the context. Called from SendMessageService's Flux.doFinally(...) so the same request-scoped bean instance cannot accidentally carry state from an aborted turn into the next one (request scope already guarantees fresh state per HTTP request, but explicit cleanup is the simpler invariant to reason about).
